title: 99 Nights in the Forest
genre: Roblox co-op survival horror / crafting & base defence (survive 99 nights around a campfire, rescue lost children, classes)
release_date: 2025-03 (Roblox) – place created 2025-03-04 [ESTIMATE – Rolimons creation date]; press says it 'came out in March 2025'. Exact public launch day: no data. Viral surge summer–autumn 2025; all-time peak 2025-10-04.
window_note: in window (March 2025 launch; viral mid/late 2025; still a top Roblox game in 2026; film deal 2026)
developer: Grandma's Favourite Games – Alec Kieft (aka 'Cracky4'), Matthew Hufton, Cameron Angland
team_size: 3 founders/developers [CONFIRMED – NZ Herald and Stuff, 2026]. Any additional contractors/staff: no data (no headcount found in 7 searches).
developer_background: Three friends who met on Roblox as 13-year-olds through a Roblox group/war clan; now develop games full-time [CONFIRMED – Stuff/PC Gamer]. 99 Nights started as a joke/bet – Kieft: 'If the game gets 80,000 players, I'll buy a Porsche' – meant as a fun one-week project while all three were in the same town [CONFIRMED – Stuff]. Close friends/collaborators of Jandel (Splitting Point, Grow a Garden) but a separate studio. Hufton says there is 'serious money' on Roblox (NZ Herald). Not their first Roblox project, but their breakout hit.
publisher: self-published (Grandma's Favourite Games on Roblox); no operator/publisher stake reported.
platforms_and_store_links: Roblox (PC, Mac, iOS, Android, Xbox, PlayStation, Meta Quest via Roblox client): https://www.roblox.com/games/79546208627805/99-Nights-in-the-Forest ; Rolimons: https://www.rolimons.com/game/79546208627805 ; RoMonitor: https://romonitorstats.com/experience/79546208627805/ ; also a Fortnite crossover ('Fortnite Override') reported by GamesBeat.
business_model: Free-to-play Roblox experience; Diamonds premium currency (earned in play, purchasable via Robux developer products) used to unlock classes; event currencies (e.g. Candy Canes for the Gifting Elf class, Christmas 2025); cosmetic items, limited-time shop offers, game passes; Roblox Premium payouts; promo codes for gems. IP licensing: feature film at 20th Century Studios (Disney) – founders are executive producers [CONFIRMED – Deadline/Variety, April 2026].
units_or_downloads: 29,896,362,267 lifetime visits; 9,785,509 favourites [ESTIMATE – Rolimons snapshot, ~Sep/Oct 2026]; RoMonitor ~9.81M favourites. Earlier: 26B visits as of April 2026 (press via Wikipedia list); 28.6B (profitable.app, 2026-07-30); >10B visits within a few months of launch (Newzoo via GameDev Reports). 1–14 Sept 2025 averaged 137M daily visits vs 108M for Grow a Garden [ESTIMATE – third-party analysis cited in search results]. Seventh most-played Roblox game of all time [CONFIRMED-as-reported – NZ Herald, 2026].
peak_concurrent_players: 14,153,173 on 2025-10-04 [ESTIMATE – Rolimons all-time peak]; reported as 14.2M by PC Gamer and Wikipedia, ~14M by NZ Herald – third-highest all-time Roblox peak at the time. Recent: 30-day peak ~1.78M, 24-hour peak 257,699 [ESTIMATE – Rolimons, ~Sep/Oct 2026]; RoMonitor shows a 1.84M range peak and 174.67k average CCU (~Oct 2026).
steam_reviews: n/a (Roblox). Roblox rating ≈ 90.5% positive (90.489%) [ESTIMATE – Rolimons, ~Sep/Oct 2026; RoMonitor 90.49–90.83%]; raw like/dislike counts: no data.
gross_revenue: No developer-reported figure (no data from the studio). Trackers: profitable.app $228.1M lifetime model, $4.2M last 30 days (2026-07-30) – generic visits-based model, effectively creator-side value, likely overstated; RoWatcher ~$1.27M/month (~$15.2M/yr, confidence 0.6, undated). Own estimate of lifetime consumer spend (Mar 2025–Sep 2026): ~$90M–$240M [ESTIMATE – 29.9B visits × ~$0.003–0.008 consumer spend per visit, the band implied by my Grow a Garden/Steal a Brainrot estimates; lower end favoured because monetization is mainly class unlocks/diamonds rather than pay-to-progress].
net_revenue: ≈ 25–30% of consumer spend → ~$25M–$70M lifetime to the three founders [ESTIMATE – spec Roblox method: ~70% creator share, DevEx ≈ $0.0038/Robux]. Self-published, so no publisher split; NZ tax not deducted.
production_cost: Original prototype: ~1 week by 3 people as a fun project – opportunity cost only (~3 × 0.25 month × $6k ≈ $4.5k) [ESTIMATE – spec method, NZ lean-indie rate]. Live-ops since launch (weekly updates in 2025): ~3 people × ~18 months × $6k ≈ $0.3M [ESTIMATE – assumes no extra staff; contractors unknown]. Hosting paid by Roblox.
development_time: Initial build intended as a ~one-week project [CONFIRMED – Stuff, founders' account]; then a strict weekly update schedule through 2025; Kieft later said the game 'hasn't fallen off a cliff' after weekly updates stopped [CONFIRMED – PC Gamer interview]. By ~Oct 2026 updates had slowed (PC Gamer codes page notes no new updates lately).
why_popular: Clear, memorable goal in the title (survive 99 nights) with a built-in progression counter that invites 'how far did you get?' sharing. Co-op loop: chop trees and gather by day, feed/upgrade the campfire, craft defences and tools, survive night attacks by The Deer (a horror monster), cultists and wolves; rescue four missing children hidden in caves; tame animals. Light horror + friends = social screams that are fun to stream and clip, while the base-building downtime leaves room to chat. Replayability from classes (unlocked with diamonds), badges (e.g. secret 'Humiliation' badge), seasonal events (Christmas 2025 classes) and weekly updates in 2025. Kid-friendly horror on the platform where kids already are – Kieft: 'Kids are on Roblox, and that's where the players are.' Won Best Adventure Experience and Best Horror Experience at the 2025 Roblox Innovation Awards.
marketing_channels: Roblox algorithmic discovery (high retention/co-op sessions), Roblox YouTubers/streamers and short-form clips (horror reactions) – no source specifically credits TikTok, so this is an inference; weekly update cadence; Roblox Innovation Awards and RDC stage appearance; Fortnite crossover (Fortnite Override); Hollywood film deal coverage (Deadline/Variety, 2026) keeps the IP in the news.
art_style: Stylised low-poly Roblox forest with dark night lighting, fog and flashlight cones; simple character models; creepy-but-kid-safe monster designs (The Deer).
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write Luau for day/night cycle with a night counter, resource gathering, inventory and crafting recipes, campfire fuel/upgrade system, base building/placement, NPC enemy AI (PathfindingService, line-of-sight rules for The Deer), rescue objectives, classes/diamonds currency, taming, DataStore persistence and MarketplaceService products; Roblox handles multiplayer replication and servers, so co-op is cheap; Roblox Assistant + Claude Code (Rojo) are strong at Luau; free Creator Store trees/rocks/props; Meshy/Tripo for monsters and props; ElevenLabs for horror SFX/ambience; Suno for music. AI cannot: tune horror pacing and night difficulty, balance 99 nights of progression, make monster encounters feel scary but fair for kids, run weekly content for months, or build a creator/streamer audience. More interlocking systems than Grow a Garden/Steal a Brainrot (combat, AI, crafting, building), so 1–3 months to MVP-plus, hence 4 rather than 5. Copycats flood quickly (Rolimons lists many '99 Nights' clones, tycoons and modded versions). Toolset: Roblox Studio + Luau + Rojo + Claude Code, Roblox Assistant, Creator Store, Meshy/Tripo (3D), Midjourney/Scenario (thumbnails/icons), ElevenLabs SFX, Suno music, Roblox Ads/Sponsored Experiences.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, ~$100–$500 (Claude Pro/Max $20–$100/mo, 3D gen $20–$60/mo, audio $10–$30/mo; Roblox Studio free, no store fee; excludes the developer's own living costs)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 3–6 months, ~$2,000–$10,000 (AI tools $60–$250/mo, freelance monster/character modelling and animation $500–$3,000, thumbnail art $200–$1,000, Roblox Ads/Sponsored Experiences and creator promos $1,000–$5,000). Weekly updates expected after launch. Excludes own living costs.

data_conflicts: Peak CCU: 14,153,173 on 2025-10-04 (Rolimons) vs 14.2M (PC Gamer/Wikipedia) vs ~14M (NZ Herald) – same peak, rounded differently; chose 14.15M. Release date: Rolimons place-creation date 2025-03-04 vs 'March 2025' in press; the exact public launch day was not found (creation date ≠ public launch). Visits: 26B (Apr 2026) → 28.6B (Jul 2026, profitable.app) → 29.9B (~Oct 2026, Rolimons) – consistent growth, not a conflict. Revenue: RoWatcher ~$15M/yr vs profitable.app $228M lifetime / $4.2M per 30 days – an order-of-magnitude gap between trackers; I used my own range labelled ESTIMATE. A '$1 billion' figure in NZ coverage refers to the whole NZ games industry, not this game or the film deal. Recent CCU: Rolimons 30-day peak 1.78M vs RoMonitor 1.84M range peak (different windows).
notes: Film: 20th Century Studios (Disney) won the theatrical rights in a competitive bid (announced April 2026); Josh Cooley attached to write and Sam Raimi to produce (Deadline, Sept 2026); founders are executive producers. Awards: Best Adventure Experience and Best Horror Experience, 2025 Roblox Innovation Awards. Cross-platform: a 99 Nights crossover into Fortnite (Fortnite Override) met mixed reactions. Strongest 'tiny team' story of the three Group B Roblox titles: 3 self-published friends, no operator studio stake, a one-week fun project → 14M CCU and a Hollywood deal. Lessons for a solo creator: (1) a numeric goal in the title ('99 nights') is a hook by itself; (2) co-op horror with friends creates shareable moments without needing PvP; (3) weekly updates mattered early, but retention held even after they stopped; (4) Roblox's audience scale ('kids are on Roblox') beats Steam for this genre; (5) expect clones within days – Rolimons lists many '99 Nights' tycoons, modded and roleplay copies.
